newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end near lows in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end near lows in quiet trade.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2331 -11 US 30yr cl 6.84 +0.02
*Stocks closed near their lows in quiet trade after the Dow fell on Monday. Volume 361.5 million shares, value A$636.2 million, 1,066 stocks traded, 331 steady, 262 rises, 473 falls

Australian shares drifted down to end near their lows on Tuesday as investors showed caution ahead of the release of key U.S. economic data later this week and after the Dow and base metals prices softened on Monday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed down 11.1 points at 2,323.0, just off its intra-day low of 2,320.6.
The December share price index ended 11 points lower at 2,331 and at an eight point premium to the underlying index.
The market ended lower across the board with the industrial sector finishing slightly weaker than the resources sector.
"It just drifted down -- everyone's waiting for the numbers out of the United States," said Macquarie Equities director Michael Coombes.
The U.S. third quarter employment cost index and October consumer confidence are due later on Tuesday, U.S. GDP is due on on Wednesday and payrolls data on Friday.
"There's a fairly nervous tone in the market, with people waiting for, one, Wall street to provide some direction and, two, an interest rate cut next week," Coombes said.
"If they don't happen it will be a bloodbath."

Brokers said the interest rate-sensitive stocks also adopted the weak tone evident in the bond markets later in the day on disappointment over a government bond tender and some nervousness about the long-awaited but as yet unseen rate cut.
"Overall it was a pretty disappointing day," said another senior Sydney broker.
"The bond market was poor so some of the interest rate sensitive stocks fell away," he said.
The Australian Banking and Finance Shares index fell 6.3 points or 0.2 percent to 3,762.4. National Australia Bank Ltd closed down 11 cents at A$13.47.
